not_claimed: Initial licensing application fee for DD group homes, renewal fees, and any inspection or survey fees. A secondary site says $750 and a DBHDS page lists $500, but the $500 is for children's residential providers. Neither is confirmed for adult DD group homes, so the model carries these as unverified operator estimates only.

Rule-stated processing and decision timelines for initial DD group home licenses. None were found in 12VAC35-105-40 or -50. The report gives the verified steps and the 6-month conditional license term only.

Staffing ratios and awake-overnight rules for group homes. 12VAC35-105-590 requires a written staffing plan sized to evacuate all residents. No numeric ratio was verified, so staffing in the model is an operator estimate tied to Tier level, not a cited ratio.
Pre-service and annual training hours, and administrator/manager qualification and training hours (12VAC35-105-200, -410, -440, -450). A secondary '40 hours' figure was not verified.

Any bed cap in 12VAC35-105 for DD group homes. The only source there is the 'eight or fewer residents' definition [S25]. The Medicaid six-licensed-bed limit in 12VAC30-122-390 was verified on the official LIS page [S28].
Zoning, siting and local land-use requirements for group homes in specific localities.
Required insurance minimums (general/professional liability, abuse and molestation, auto, property, workers' comp limits) for DBHDS or DMAS providers. Premiums in the model are operator estimates.
Building, fire and life-safety inspection requirements (12VAC35-105-260, -320) and onsite review frequency (12VAC35-105-70).

Tier rates for 5- to 7-person homes, and Tiers 2–4 for 8- and 12-person homes (Tier 3 for 4 or fewer persons is in the rates appendix). The tier assignment criteria (12VAC30-122-210) were not summarized.

Whether the 2% 7/1/2026 group home increase is anything other than what the DMAS rate file change log states. A floor-approved SB30 amendment text is not proof of enactment. A further 4.6% on January 1, 2027 appears only as member-request amendments and is not confirmed as enacted. The enacted Item 291 raises only personal care, respite and companion rates (4% on 1/1/2027), not group home.

Final per-person revenue per day actually paid. DMAS pays only for services not covered by the patient pay amount, and the patient pay offset for individual residents was not quantified. The 344-billing-day basis is shown in the rate file but its exact conversion to monthly billing units beyond that was not verified.

Statewide provider market share, competitor names, number of licensed DD group home providers or locations by bed size today (only 2022 counts: 1,427 providers, 3,645 services, 712 adult residential services at 2,139 locations), and occupancy or vacancy rates for DD group homes. No current public source was found.
Share of DD waiver recipients aged 65+, and referral-source breakdowns (hospitals, schools, CSBs, families) for group home placements.

Why waitlist figures differ across sources (14,226 DMAS May 2026; 14,258 DBHDS reporting period 2025; 14,168–15,472 in a secondary KFF compilation). The report cites DMAS/VBPD and the DBHDS Item 295 K report only. The publication date of the Item 295 K report is also unconfirmed, because the transmittal letter and the cover date disagree.

Occupation-level statewide BLS OEWS May 2025 wages for direct support professionals/nursing assistants, LPNs, RNs, cooks and administrators. Only Richmond and Virginia Beach MSA group-level means (personal care and service $18.47 Richmond, $17.87 Virginia Beach; healthcare support $18.48 Virginia Beach; management $71.81 Richmond) and the statewide all-occupation mean annual wage of $74,040 were retrieved. Model wages must be labeled operator estimates unless supported by those figures. Northern Virginia metro wages were not retrieved.

Virginia 2027 minimum wage ($13.75) and any later scheduled step: only secondary sources were found, and the LIS statute text was not verified. No local minimum above the state rate was found, from a secondary source.

Official VEC confirmation of the 2026 UI taxable wage base ($8,000) and add-on charges. The VEC page confirms only the 2.5% initial new-employer base rate and the 0.1%–6.2% range. Secondary sources conflict on the add-on charges.
Official SCC fee schedule for Articles of Organization ($100) and the LLC annual registration fee ($50). Both come from secondary sites and the SCC site was not fetched.

Approved Virginia workers' compensation loss cost changes. NCCI's proposed -5.6% filing (effective 4/1/2027) is pending, a secondary source cites -7.7% for 4/1/2026 and conflicts with the NCCI filing, and the workers' comp coverage trigger (3+ employees) comes from a secondary source. Verify Va. Code Title 65.2.

HUD FY2026/FY2027 Fair Market Rents from huduser.gov for Virginia metros, and any commercial or group-home-suitable rent benchmark. Secondary figures conflict ($1,350 vs. $1,400 for a 2BR in Hampton Roads), and Northern Virginia and Richmond rents were not retrieved. Rent in the model must be an operator estimate, verify locally.

Private-pay price benchmark for shared DD group homes. The Genworth/CareScout 2024 Virginia assisted living median ($78,150/year, about $6,513/month) measures private one-bedroom units in assisted living communities, not group homes. A secondary summary's $6,050/month does not reconcile with it. The report treats DD group homes as Medicaid-waiver funded and does not model private pay.

Any Virginia SSI state supplement for group home residents (only the federal $994 SSI rate was verified), and the room-and-board amount a resident can be charged. DMAS states room and board is not reimbursed, but no Virginia cap or standard amount was found.

Virginia-specific DMAS provider enrollment steps and any state-level enrollment fee. Only the federal CY2026 $750 fee for institutional providers was verified, and whether it applies to group home providers is stated in the DMAS enrollment notice.

Status and timing of DBHDS's restructuring of Chapter 105 into a general chapter plus service-specific chapters, including the Residential and Inpatient chapter. The general-chapter action was at the Proposed stage with Attorney General review (date not shown), and Town Hall numbering conflicts (12VAC35-270 vs. 12VAC35-106) were seen. occupancy.rationale: Share of licensed beds filled with a DMAS-authorized resident. These percentages are operator assumptions, not sourced statistics: no public vacancy or occupancy data for Virginia DD group homes was found. Demand is large (DD waiver waitlist 14,226 in May 2026; 2,632 Priority One on Sept. 21, 2026) [S36][S37]. But a new provider is not handed referrals. The individual or family chooses a provider through the CSB support coordinator, and DMAS pays only after a service authorization is in place [S20][S42]. DMAS rates are set on a 344-billing-day basis [S14]. The model bills 28.67 days per resident per month (344 ÷ 12) and then applies this bed-fill percentage for vacancy between placements. Whether 344 is a billing cap or only a rate-setting basis was not verified, so the combined effect of the two adjustments on revenue is uncertain.

configurations.label: One 4-bed DD group home, Tier 1 residents, Rest of State (ROS) rates
configurations.notes: Launch model. A new provider on a conditional license is limited to a single location and no more than four individuals for up to six months (12 months total with renewals), cannot add services or locations during that period, and DBHDS allows one active conditional license per provider [S9][S26][S10]. Rates are Rest of State (everything outside Northern Virginia). A Northern Virginia home is not modeled because NOVA wages and rents were not retrieved. NOVA rates are in the rates appendix. Group home residential is paid only for settings with no more than six licensed beds. Only larger homes that became DD Waiver providers before March 31, 2021 are grandfathered, and a change of ownership removes that status [S28]. Verified rates cover homes of 4 or fewer, so every configuration uses 4-bed homes. Tier assignment comes from the resident's authorization, not from operator choice [S14].

staffing.notes: 1,095 h/month = 36 staff-hours/day × 30.42. This is an operator estimate: no numeric ratio or awake-overnight rule was verified. 12VAC35-105-590 requires a written staffing plan with enough staff to evacuate all residents safely [S4], and a group home is a 24-hour supervised service [S25]. If your plan requires two overnight staff, add about 365 h/month (roughly $8,000/month loaded), which would erase this home's margin. sections.executive_summary:
Virginia does not have a stand-alone 'DD group home' license under another name. The model is a **DBHDS-licensed developmental disability residential group home service** under 12VAC35-105, paid by DMAS as **Group Home Residential (HCPCS H2022)** under the DD Waivers: Community Living (CL), Family & Individual Supports (FIS) and Building Independence (BI) [S1][S5][S6][S14]. The waiver requires a DBHDS group home license (or a DSS-approved adult foster care home) and a current DMAS provider participation agreement [S2][S27][S28]. DBHDS defines a group home as a congregate service with 24-hour supervision in a community home of eight or fewer residents [S25].

**Money flows fee-for-service from DMAS, not through managed care.** DMAS says DD waiver benefits are carved out of managed care and managed directly by DMAS, and that this holds for members in Cardinal Care [S15][S16]. Rates in effect 7/1/2026 are per diem by home size, tier and region. For homes of 4 or fewer persons: Tier 1 is **$391.16 NOVA / $347.17 Rest of State (ROS)**, Tier 2 is **$467.16 / $414.60**, Tier 3 is **$515.37 / $457.37**, and Tier 4 is **$616.89 / $547.46** [S14]. DMAS records a 2% increase for H2022 effective 7/1/2026 [S14][S17]. Room and board is not reimbursed [S18], and DMAS pays only for the part of the service not covered by the resident's patient pay [S19].

**Demand is large, but placement is not guaranteed.** DMAS data cited by the Virginia Board for People with Disabilities put the DD waiver waitlist at 14,226 in May 2026 [S36]. DBHDS reported 2,632 people on the Priority One list on September 21, 2026 and 21,479 funded slots across the three waivers at the end of FY2026 [S37]. In FY2026, 4,828 individuals received the 4-or-fewer-person group home service, with $657,823,485 in spending [S37]. A new provider still gets no referral pipeline. Residents are matched through CSB support coordinators, and DMAS pays only once a service authorization is in place [S20][S42].

**The economics are thin and size-sensitive.** At the default 92% bed-fill (an operator assumption), the modeled single 4-bed ROS homes earn about **$4,654 a month (11.9% margin) at Tier 1**, **$3,712 (8.0%) at Tier 2** and **$1,617 (2.7%) at Tier 4**. A new provider can open only one home of up to four residents during the conditional license period, so launch economics are those of a single home [S9][S26]. Two- and three-home agencies are expansion scenarios that can start only after a full license is issued. Break-even bed-fill runs from 80.5% (Tier 1) to 89.5% (Tier 4). Staffing hours are operator estimates because no numeric ratio was verified, so these results are a planning range, not a forecast. Initial licensing fees, renewal fees, processing timelines and insurance minimums could not be verified and are listed in the 'not claimed' section.
sections.service_model:
**Who is served.** Adults (18+) with developmental disabilities who hold a DD waiver slot and need residential supports. The Community Living waiver can fund 24/7 supports through licensed services for people with complex medical or behavioral needs [S2]. FIS and BI are the other two DD waivers, and DMAS lists all three as payers of group home residential services [S14][S42]. Group home residential is one of several residential options. Sponsored Residential, a family-style alternative, recorded $350,439,439 in FY2026 spending for 3,097 individuals [S37]. Supported Living Residential (H0043) is a separate per-diem service with its own rates [S14].

**The model.** A group home is a congregate service with 24-hour supervision in a community-based home of eight or fewer residents [S25]. DBHDS also describes group homes as typically serving eight or fewer residents [S48], which is descriptive and not a licensing cap. Medicaid reimbursement for group home residential service is limited to settings of no more than six licensed beds (12VAC30-122-390 A). Only larger homes that became DD Waiver providers before March 31, 2021 are grandfathered, and a change of ownership makes the home a new setting subject to the six-bed limit [S28]. The DMAS rate file lists homes from 4-or-fewer up to 12 persons, with the per-diem falling as home size rises (Tier 1 ROS: $347.17 for 4 or fewer, $281.88 for 8 persons, $242.64 for 12 persons) [S14]. The 7- to 12-person rates are not available to new providers. Every modeled configuration therefore uses 4-bed homes.

**Regulatory framework.** Licensing is under 12VAC35-105, adopted under Va. Code §§ 37.2-203, 37.2-400 and 37.2-404 [S4][S43]. Waiver service rules are in 12VAC30-122 (service definition at -390, payment tiers at -210, provider training at -180) [S14][S27][S28]. Group homes must keep no more than two individuals sharing a bedroom, per the group home definition text in the Register. Confirm current wording after the June 2025 amendments [S25][S11]. The 2025 regulatory-reduction amendments took effect in June 2025 (June 18 per the Register; DBHDS shows 6/19/25) [S1][S11].

**Settings and rights.** New DD group home residential providers must be in full compliance with the CMS HCBS settings rules before completing the DMAS participation agreement, and DBHDS requires human-rights-compliant policies before licensure [S2]. EVV is not required for individuals in a DBHDS-licensed group home, per the DMAS EVV FAQ [S23]. EVV does apply to some other DMAS services [S22].
sections.licensing_pathway:
**Overview.** Licensure runs through DBHDS's Office of Licensing and the **CONNECT** portal, where new applications and modifications are submitted electronically [S1]. DBHDS lists a developmental disability residential group home service for adults as the license type [S6]. Two items could not be verified: **the initial application fee** and **rule-stated decision timelines**. They were not found in 12VAC35-105-40 or -50 (see 'not claimed').

**Step-by-step pathway**

1. **Form the entity and get an EIN and NPI.** A Virginia LLC filing is reported at $100 with a $50 annual registration fee. Both figures are from secondary sources, so confirm them on the SCC site [S54][S55]. Out-of-state applicants need a real in-state physical location for DMAS enrollment. A P.O. box or mailbox store does not suffice [S2].
2. **Secure the home.** A 4-bedroom home is the planning unit in this model. No more than two residents may share a bedroom [S25]. Zoning, fire and life-safety requirements were not verified and must be checked locally.
3. **Prepare the application.** Providers submit an application listing each service. For each service the application needs a staffing plan, employee credentials and job descriptions, a service description and a records management policy. It also needs **a first-year working budget with a revenue plan** [S7][S26]. Non-government applicants must show **funds or a line of credit sufficient to cover at least 90 days of operating expenses** [S7].
4. **Human rights policies.** Before receiving a DBHDS license, new providers must develop policies that comply with the Human Rights Regulations. The Complaint Resolution Policy and Human Rights Compliance Verification Checklist go to the Office of Human Rights [S2].
5. **Background checks.** Fingerprint-based criminal history checks apply to employees, students, interns, volunteers and contractors, and results must be received before the person works. A Central Registry (child abuse and neglect) check is also required [S3]. Confirm check fees and payment instructions with the DBHDS Background Investigations Unit.
6. **Conditional license.** A conditional license shall not exceed six months. During that period a provider may not add services or locations, and a group home provider is limited to a single location and no more than four individuals [S9][S26]. DBHDS's January 2026 memo limits a provider to one active conditional license at a time [S10]. A conditional license runs 12 months in total including renewals [S9]. Plan for one home at launch; a second home can be opened only after a full license is issued.
7. **Full license.** A full license may be granted for up to three years [S9]. A change of ownership requires a new application and a new license [S9].
8. **DMAS enrollment.** Group home residential providers must hold a current DMAS provider participation agreement [S27]. HCBS settings compliance (with a DMAS compliance letter) comes before signing the agreement [S2]. The federal application fee for institutional providers is $750 for applications submitted in calendar 2026. DMAS says it may be required at application, and the enrollment notice states whether it applies [S24][S15].
9. **Authorization and billing.** Service authorization requests go through the DBHDS Waiver Management System, submitted by the individual's support coordinator [S20].

**Ongoing deadlines.** DBHDS guidance says to file renewals at least 30 calendar days before the license expires, or DMAS claims may be denied. Modification applications (service or location changes) should be filed at least 30 days before the proposed change [S8]. Plan staff screening against federal exclusion lists monthly, with documentation [S2].

**Pending change.** DBHDS is restructuring Chapter 105 into one general chapter plus service-specific chapters, including a residential chapter. The general chapter action was at the Proposed stage with Attorney General review in progress, with no date shown [S12][S13]. The pathway above could change, so recheck 12VAC35-105 before filing.
sections.reimbursement:
**How money flows.** DD waiver services are paid **fee-for-service by DMAS**. DMAS states that DD waiver benefits are carved out of managed care and managed directly by DMAS, and that members enrolled in Cardinal Care keep DD waiver services in Medicaid fee-for-service [S15][S16]. There are no managed care plan rates to negotiate. The provider bills DMAS directly under a participation agreement [S27]. Before billing, the individual's support coordinator submits a service authorization request through the DBHDS Waiver Management System [S20].

**Rates (effective 7/1/2026, per diem, H2022 by size modifier).** The DMAS rate file bills group home residential under H2022, with modifiers UA (4 or fewer), U2 (5), U3 (6), U4 (7), U5 (8), U6 (9), U7 (10), U8 (11) and U9 (12), on a 344-billing-day per diem basis [S14].

| 4 or fewer persons | NOVA | ROS |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | $391.16 | $347.17 |
| Tier 2 | $467.16 | $414.60 |
| Tier 3 | $515.37 | $457.37 |
| Tier 4 (highest published) | $616.89 | $547.46 |

Tier rates for 5- to 7-person homes were not retrieved. Reference points for larger homes (Tier 1): 8 persons NOVA $318.03 / ROS $281.88; 12 persons NOVA $273.53 / ROS $242.64 [S14]. These larger-home rates are not available to new providers, because Medicaid reimburses no more than six licensed beds and grandfathers only homes enrolled before March 31, 2021 [S28]. Tiers are set under 12VAC30-122-210 [S14]. The tier is tied to the resident's authorization and is not a choice the operator makes. The tier criteria were not summarized in this research.

**Rate changes.** DMAS's change log records a 2% increase for group home residential H2022 effective 7/1/2026, and a DMAS bulletin says July 1, 2026 DD waiver rates were updated under Item 291 of the 2026 Appropriation Act [S14][S17]. A further 4.6% group home increase on January 1, 2027 appears only in member-request amendment text and its enactment is unconfirmed [S39][S45]. The enacted Item 291 raises personal care, respite and companion rates 4% on 1/1/2027, and does not list group home [S40]. The model uses 7/1/2026 rates only. DMAS is also requesting authority for DD and HCBS waiver amendments effective 1/1/2027 [S41].

**What the rate does not cover.** DMAS will not reimburse providers for room and board [S18]. The resident (usually through SSI, $994 per month federal benefit rate in 2026 [S21]) pays it. No Virginia cap, standard amount or state SSI supplement was verified. The model assumes $700 a month per resident, about 70% of the federal SSI benefit, so the resident keeps spending money. This is an operator estimate and each resident's income must be checked. DMAS also reimburses only services not covered by the patient pay amount [S19]. The patient pay effect on individual residents was not quantified, so net DMAS receipts could be lower than the modeled rate for residents with patient pay.

**Units.** The model bills 28.67 days per resident per month (344 ÷ 12) from the rate file's 344-billing-day basis [S14]. Whether 344 is an annual billing cap or only a rate-setting basis was not verified. Check with DMAS how billable days are counted before relying on the figures, because the answer could change revenue in either direction.
sections.demand:
**Waitlist and slots.** DMAS data cited by the Virginia Board for People with Disabilities put the DD waiver waitlist at **14,226** in May 2026 [S36]. DBHDS reported **2,632** on the Priority One list (the group needing services soonest) as of September 21, 2026 [S37]. A DBHDS January 2026 document reported 14,258 total and 2,727 Priority One for a 2025 reporting period [S38]. A secondary KFF compilation shows 14,168–15,472 and the reason for the gaps is not documented, so this report relies on the DMAS and DBHDS figures. Across the three waivers the Commonwealth had **21,479 funded slots** at the close of FY2026 [S37].

**New and turnover slots.** The 2024 General Assembly funded 1,720 new slots for each fiscal year of the biennium [S37]. They are allocated to the 40 CSBs using population, Medicaid-eligible share and each CSB's share of Priority One people [S37]. By September 8, 2026, 77% of FY2026 new-slot recipients had at least one service authorized, up from 61% a year earlier [S37]. Vacated slots were reassigned from the statewide waitlist 635 times and total turnover was 861 in FY2026, which DBHDS said falls far short of the Priority One need [S37]. Emergency slots assigned were 60, 14 fewer than FY2025, and reserve slots assigned (waiver-to-waiver moves) were 226 [S37]. The introduced 2026 budget language would authorize 12,520 Community Living slots as of July 1, 2026 [S46], and its final enacted figure was not verified.

**Existing group home utilization.** In FY2026, 4,828 individuals received the 4-or-fewer-person group home residential service ($657,823,485 in spending), and 736 individuals received the 5-person service ($74,819,625). Counts are per service, so a person can appear under several services [S37]. The average FY2026 cost per person on the Community Living waiver was reported as $143,388 [S37].

**How referrals work.** The first step for DD waiver access is contacting the local CSB [S42]. A new home fills through CSB support coordinators, individual and family choice, slot movements and transfers. The sponsor of a slot pays no referral fee, and no referral-source breakdown (hospitals, schools, CSBs, families) was found. Neither the share of waiver recipients aged 65+ nor any occupancy or vacancy data for DD group homes was found, so bed-fill in the model is an assumption (92% default, 88% conservative, 96% optimistic) and not a statistic.
sections.operations:
**Staffing plan.** 12VAC35-105-590 requires a written staffing plan covering the types, roles and numbers of staff, with an adequate number of staff to safely evacuate all individuals in an emergency [S4]. DD services supervision must be provided by a person with at least one year of documented DD experience. A bachelor's degree in a human services field may be used with experience substituting for education [S4]. **No numeric staffing ratio or awake-overnight rule was verified.** The model therefore uses operator-estimated coverage hours for each tier: 36 staff-hours a day for Tier 1 (2 awake on day shift, 1 overnight), 48 for Tier 2 (3 and 1), and 72 for Tier 4 (4 and 2). Your licensed staffing plan and each resident's authorized supports drive actual hours.

**Management.** The model includes a half-time program director/DD services supervisor ($27,500 a year, operator estimate) for each single home, scaling to a full-time director, an assistant supervisor and a billing/records coordinator in the multi-home configurations. Administrator qualifications and training hours (12VAC35-105-200, -410) were not verified.

**Training and screening.** Staff providing group home residential service must meet the training and competency requirements in 12VAC30-122-180 [S27]. Pre-service and annual training hours were not verified (a secondary '40 hours' figure was not confirmed). Fingerprint criminal history checks and the Central Registry check must be received before a person works [S3]. Providers must screen and document all new and existing employees and contractors against federal exclusion lists monthly [S2].

**Systems.** Providers need CONNECT portal access for licensing [S1]. They also need DMAS billing capability and a records system. Service authorizations arrive through the support coordinator's submission in the DBHDS Waiver Management System [S20]. EVV is not required for individuals in a DBHDS-licensed group home [S23], but confirm this applies to every service you bill. Keep records of exclusion screening, background checks and human rights policy approvals.

**Home standards.** Use bedrooms with no more than two residents each [S25]. Building, fire and life-safety rules (12VAC35-105-260, -320), onsite review frequency (-70) and local zoning were not retrieved. Meet your locality's requirements and fire marshal inspections before applying.
sections.market_conditions:
**Supply.** No current public count of licensed DD group home providers or locations by size was found. The most recent figures are from a September 2022 DBHDS presentation: 1,427 licensed providers, 3,645 licensed services and 11,324 licensed locations across all DBHDS settings, with 712 adult residential services at 2,139 adult residential service locations [S47]. DBHDS publishes a monthly list of licensed DD residential sites with each site's approved bed capacity [S1], which is the best way to size your local competition. Market shares and competitor names are not claimed.

**Wages.** Virginia's minimum wage is **$12.77 an hour in 2026** [S29]. A secondary source says it is scheduled to rise to $13.75 on January 1, 2027 (verify the statute on LIS) [S50], and another says no Virginia city or county sets a higher local minimum [S51]. The model uses **$18.47 an hour** for direct support staff, the Richmond MSA mean for personal care and service occupations (BLS, May 2025) [S30]. This is a group-level proxy because occupation-level DSP wages were not retrieved. The Virginia Beach-Chesapeake-Norfolk figure for the same group is $17.87, and its healthcare support mean is $18.48 [S31]. Richmond management occupations average $71.81 an hour [S30], and the statewide all-occupation mean annual wage is $74,040 [S32]. Management and supervisor salaries in the model ($55,000 full-time, $40,000 for billing) are operator estimates. Northern Virginia wages were not retrieved, which is why NOVA homes are not modeled even though NOVA rates are higher.

**Rent.** Rent in the model is $2,500 per 4-bedroom home, based on a secondary summary of FY2026 HUD Fair Market Rent for a 4-bedroom in the Virginia Beach-Norfolk area ($2,290) plus an operator-estimate premium [S57]. Secondary sources conflict on Hampton Roads FMR, and the official HUD table was not confirmed. The wage data are Richmond-based while the rent proxy is Hampton Roads. Use quotes from your actual locality.

**Payroll and insurance.** New Virginia employers start at a 2.5% base unemployment rate plus add-ons, and normal base rates run 0.1%–6.2% [S33]. The $8,000 wage base and add-on charges come from conflicting secondary sources [S52][S53]. Workers' comp: NCCI's July 2026 filing proposes a −5.6% change to voluntary loss costs effective 4/1/2027, which is pending [S49]. Liability and abuse/molestation insurance minimums were not found, so insurance premiums are operator estimates.

**Private pay.** The model does not include private pay. The Genworth/CareScout 2024 Virginia assisted living median ($78,150 a year, about $6,513 a month) measures private units in assisted living communities, not DD group homes [S34]. A secondary summary's $6,050 a month does not reconcile with it. For reference only, CareScout's 2025 national assisted living median is $6,200 a month [S35].
sections.financial_narrative:
**How the P&L is built.** Revenue per resident is the DMAS per diem × 28.67 billing days (344 ÷ 12) plus $700 a month of resident-paid room and board [S14][S21]. Revenue is then scaled by bed-fill (92% default). Costs are direct support hours at $18.47 [S30], supervisory and billing salaries, payroll burden of 19.5% (8.5% taxes, 5% workers' comp, 6% benefits, with the last two operator estimates), fixed home costs (rent, utilities, maintenance, vehicle, insurance, internet) sized per home, and per-resident food, supplies and software. Rent and staffing do not fall when a bed is empty. Direct support hours are priced at straight wage, with no overtime, relief coverage or paid leave.

**Launch configurations: one 4-bed home at 92% bed-fill (ROS rates)**

A new provider on a conditional license is limited to one location and four individuals, and may not add locations during that period [S9][S26]. Launch economics are therefore those of a single home.

| Configuration | Net / month | Margin | Break-even bed-fill | First profit month | Cash needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| One 4-bed home, Tier 1 | $4,654 | 11.9% | 80.5% | 4 | $124,900 |
| One 4-bed home, Tier 2 (default) | $3,712 | 8.0% | 84.3% | 4 | $124,900 |
| One 4-bed home, Tier 4 | $1,617 | 2.7% | 89.5% | 4 | $124,900 |

**Expansion scenarios (only after a full license is issued; not launch economics)**

| Configuration | Net / month | Margin | Break-even bed-fill |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two 4-bed homes, Tier 2 (8 residents) | $3,286 | 3.5% | 88.6% |
| Three 4-bed homes, mixed Tiers 1/2/4 (12 residents) | $5,206 | 3.6% | 88.6% |

These expansion results assume a full license, a pipeline from several CSBs, and both or all homes staffed from month 1. They need their own timeline, ramp and cash plan, and no launch cash total is given for them.

**Key drivers.**

- **Staffing hours dominate.** The three tiers differ mostly in assumed staff-hours (1,095, 1,460 and 2,190 a month), which are operator estimates, not a cited ratio. The highest-need home earns the highest rate ($547.46) but its assumed 2,190 hours leave a margin of 2.7%. Tier 1 looks best only because its assumed coverage is the lightest. Real tier assignment comes from authorizations, so you cannot pick it.
- **Scale does not automatically help.** The expansion models add a full-time director, an assistant and a billing coordinator, so margins (3.5% and 3.6%) are below the single-home Tier 1 and Tier 2 results. Expansion pays off only with disciplined fill and overhead.
- **A single vacancy hurts.** A 4-bed home with one empty bed runs at 75% bed-fill, below the break-even of every single-home configuration (80.5%–89.5%). Each home needs at least about 3.2–3.6 beds filled on average to break even. Break-even is not a precise point because the model's day conversion is an assumption.
- **Ramp.** The model admits one resident a month. The one-home configurations first turn profitable in month 4. Cash needed is far above the first-year budget a new applicant files, and the required reserve of 90 days of operating expenses (about $100,000 for a Tier 1 home to about $175,000 for a Tier 4 home in the startup table, both one-home figures) is a licensing condition [S7].

**Sensitivities (approximate, derived from the model).**

- *Second overnight staff.* If your staffing plan needs two awake overnight staff, that adds about 365 hours a month, or roughly $8,000 a month loaded (365 h × $18.47 × 1.195). That turns the Tier 1 and Tier 2 single homes from profits of $4,654 and $3,712 to losses of about $3,300 and $4,300 a month.
- *Wage.* Using the Virginia Beach MSA wage ($17.87) instead of $18.47 would save about $785 a month in the Tier 1 home (1,095 h × $0.60 × 1.195). Wages above $18.47 reduce profit by the same arithmetic. The $18.47 is a group-level proxy and should be replaced with an occupation-level wage for your location. Even at the 2027 scheduled minimum of $13.75 [S50], the modeled wage is well above it.
- *Overtime.* Twelve-hour shifts can take full-time non-exempt staff over 40 hours a week. Overtime or relief coverage would reduce profit and is not modeled.
- *Rate.* The Tier 2 default home earns about $44,000 a month in revenue at 92% bed-fill. The proposed 4.6% increase on 1/1/2027 would add roughly $2,000 a month, but it is unconfirmed and not modeled [S39][S45].
- *Patient pay.* DMAS pays only the portion not covered by patient pay [S19]. Residents with patient pay lower receipts below the modeled figures and this was not quantified.
- *Room and board.* If a resident's income supports less than $700, revenue falls by the shortfall per resident per month. No Virginia cap or state supplement was verified.

**Path to profit.** The most reliable route is a single 4-bed home filled quickly, with a staffing plan that meets the safe-evacuation standard at the lowest compliant hours, an owner who fills the supervisor role for the first months, and a line of credit that covers the 90-day reserve. Expansion beyond one home can begin only after a full license is issued and fill is demonstrated. Rate increases, lower-cost staffing or an unverified fee reduction should not be assumed. Note that the licensing and renewal fees in the model are placeholders, so replace them once verified.
sections.risks:
- **Staffing-rule risk.** No numeric ratio was verified, so the coverage hours are estimates. A requirement or authorization that needs more awake staff (for example a second overnight person, about $8,000 a month loaded) would turn the single-home models into losses. Overtime or relief coverage for 12-hour shifts is also not modeled.
- **Tier risk.** The tier is set by the resident's authorization and the tier rates differ widely ($347.17 to $547.46 ROS). The operator cannot choose it, and higher-need residents may need nursing or behavioral support that the model does not include.
- **Vacancy and referral risk.** Despite a 14,226-person waitlist [S36], placement depends on CSB support coordinators and individual choice, and DMAS pays only after a service authorization [S20][S42]. Slot turnover (861 in FY2026) is far below Priority One need [S37]. One empty bed in four puts a home below break-even.
- **Conditional license limits.** A new provider is limited to one location and four individuals for up to six months (12 months total with renewals), cannot add services or locations during that period, and is limited to one active conditional license [S9][S26][S10]. A second or third home cannot be part of the launch plan. A change of ownership needs a new license [S9].
- **Licensing lapses.** Late renewals (under 30 days before expiration) can lead to DMAS claim denials [S8]. A late modification can disrupt service or billing.
- **Regulatory change.** The 2025 amendments took effect in June 2025, and DBHDS is restructuring Chapter 105 into a general chapter and service-specific chapters (Proposed stage) [S11][S12][S13]. The Medicaid six-licensed-bed limit applies to new providers, and the grandfathering for larger homes enrolled before March 31, 2021 ends on a change of ownership [S28].
- **Rate and budget uncertainty.** The 7/1/2026 2% increase is in the DMAS rate file [S14]. The 1/1/2027 4.6% is only proposed [S39][S45], and the enacted Item 291 increase does not list group home [S40]. DMAS is also seeking 1/1/2027 waiver amendments [S41]. How the 344-billing-day basis converts to monthly billable days is unconfirmed and could move revenue either way.
- **Cash and payment risk.** HCBS compliance must precede the DMAS agreement [S2], and no processing timeline was verified. The model's cash needs ($124,900 for one home) are large relative to monthly profit, and ramp delays add monthly fixed cost.
- **Resident income and patient pay.** DMAS does not pay room and board [S18], and patient pay offsets the DMAS payment [S19]. Revenue could be lower than modeled.
- **Wage and cost pressure.** The minimum wage is $12.77 now and a secondary source says $13.75 in 2027 [S29][S50]. The modeled DSP wage is a Richmond group-level proxy [S30], and Northern Virginia was not modeled. The $2,500 rent proxy is a Hampton Roads-based estimate from secondary data [S57].
- **Compliance risk.** Missing a monthly exclusion screening [S2], starting staff before background results [S3], or failing HCBS settings requirements can jeopardize the license and billing.
- **Insurance and workers' comp.** No required insurance minimums were found. Workers' comp coverage thresholds came from a secondary source, and the NCCI loss cost filing is pending [S49][S53].
- **Fee uncertainty.** The initial and renewal licensing fees are not verified. The placeholders in the model ($750 a year) could be wrong in either direction.
sections.recommendations:
1. **Start with one 4-bed home.** It fits the conditional license limits (one location, four individuals) and keeps the cash need near the modeled $124,900 [S9][S26]. Build the 90-day operating-expense reserve or line of credit into your plan before you file, because the application requires it [S7].
2. **Write the staffing plan to the lowest compliant level.** Draft the 12VAC35-105-590 written staffing plan with exact shifts, evacuation capacity and a supervisor with at least one year of documented DD experience [S4]. Confirm with the Office of Licensing whether one or two awake overnight staff are expected. That single answer can move the home between profit and loss.
3. **Line up referrals before you open.** Meet CSB support coordinators in the region. They hold the DD waiver entry point and the authorization process [S20][S42]. Target a first resident mix you can actually serve. Do not plan on tier choice, and have a clear view of whether you can support the needs behind a Tier 2 or Tier 4 authorization.
4. **Sequence compliance correctly.** Prepare human rights policies and send them to the Office of Human Rights [S2]. Bring the home into full HCBS settings compliance, obtain the DMAS compliance letter, and then complete the DMAS participation agreement [S2][S27]. Run fingerprint and Central Registry checks for everyone before work begins [S3], and set up monthly exclusion screening from day one [S2].
5. **Verify the unverified items before committing capital.** Ask DBHDS for the current initial and renewal fees, decision timelines and inspection fees. Obtain insurance quotes, and get a real lease quote for your locality. Check the six-licensed-bed limit on LIS, the current bedroom-sharing text, and the status of the Chapter 105 restructuring [S12][S13][S25][S28].
6. **Use ROS-based planning unless you can staff NOVA.** NOVA rates are 12–13% higher than ROS at Tier 1 and Tier 2, but NOVA wages and rents were not researched. Run your own numbers with local wages and rent before choosing the region [S14].
7. **Set room and board from each resident's actual income.** Start from the $994 SSI federal benefit [S21], check for patient pay [S19], and do not assume more than the resident can pay. The model uses $700.
8. **Do not count on rate increases.** Plan on the 7/1/2026 rates only. Treat the proposed 4.6% on 1/1/2027 as upside if it is confirmed [S39][S45].
9. **Scale only after a stable single home.** Wait for a full license, a home running above the break-even bed-fill (80.5%–89.5% depending on tier), and a billing process that works. Open additional homes one at a time and hire staff as each fills, which needs less cash than the modeled staffing of every home from month 1. Remember that the two- and three-home models earn thinner margins (3.5% and 3.6%) than the best single-home models, so more homes only pay off with disciplined fill and overhead.
10. **Keep renewal and modification calendars.** File renewals at least 30 days before expiration and modifications at least 30 days before any change [S8]. Re-check DMAS rate files and bulletins each July and January [S14][S17].

checklist.task: Confirm the correct pathway: DBHDS-licensed DD group home residential service plus a DMAS DD Waiver provider agreement
checklist.instructions: Virginia DD group homes need two approvals. The first is a DBHDS license for a 'developmental disability residential group home service for adults' under 12VAC35-105. The second is a DMAS participation agreement to bill Group Home Residential (H2022) under the CL, FIS and BI waivers. A DBHDS license alone does not pay you. DMAS requires either a DBHDS group home license or an approved adult foster care home. Do not plan on assisted living or RCFE-style rules.

checklist.task: Read the DD Waivers Prospective Provider Toolkit end to end before spending money
checklist.instructions: DBHDS publishes the Feb. 2025 toolkit. It covers licensure, human rights policy approval, CMS HCBS settings compliance, the DMAS participation agreement and the physical-presence rule. Free. Allow 1–2 days to read, and keep a checklist of every document it names.
checklist.cite: DBHDS DD Waivers Prospective Provider Toolkit (2/25/2025)

checklist.task: Form a Virginia legal entity (LLC) with the State Corporation Commission
checklist.instructions: File Articles of Organization with the SCC. A secondary source puts the filing fee at $100 and the annual registration fee at $50, and says Virginia has no LLC franchise tax. Confirm all of these on the SCC site, because it was not fetched. Have an attorney review the structure, since a DMAS and DBHDS provider carries abuse, neglect and billing liability.
checklist.cite: Va. SCC (confirm fee schedule on SCC site)

checklist.task: Obtain a federal EIN
checklist.instructions: Apply free at irs.gov. It is issued immediately online. You need it for payroll, the bank account and the DMAS enrollment packet.

checklist.task: Open a business bank account and set up bookkeeping
checklist.instructions: Keep the entity's operating money separate from residents' funds. Residents' room-and-board payments and personal funds need their own tracking. Set up accounting and payroll software or a service. The model carries about $500/month for accounting, payroll service and legal as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Register for Virginia withholding and unemployment insurance (VEC) before the first hire
checklist.instructions: New Virginia employers get an initial UI base rate of 2.5% plus add-ons until a calculated rate applies, and normal base rates run 0.1%–6.2%. The $8,000 taxable wage base and the add-on charges come from secondary sources that conflict, so confirm both with the VEC. Register with the Virginia Dept. of Taxation for withholding.

checklist.task: Arrange workers' compensation coverage
checklist.instructions: A secondary source says coverage is required at 3 or more employees, including part-time. Verify under Va. Code Title 65.2 and just buy it before hiring direct support staff. Virginia is an advisory loss-cost state, so carriers set their own multipliers. Get at least three quotes. The model uses 5% of payroll as an operator estimate. NCCI's proposed −5.6% change is pending and not approved.
checklist.cite: Va. Code Title 65.2 (verify); NCCI VA filing July 2026

checklist.task: Check local business license (BPOL), zoning and home-occupancy rules for each locality
checklist.instructions: No official source on zoning, siting or local land-use rules for group homes was found. Call the planning/zoning office of the city or county before signing any lease, and ask whether a local business license is required. Get written confirmation. Local rules vary.
checklist.cite: Local ordinances (not verified in this research)

checklist.task: If you are an out-of-state applicant, arrange a real in-state physical location
checklist.instructions: DBHDS states that a P.O. box or a mailbox store address will not satisfy the DMAS physical-presence requirement. You need a physical in-state site with a workstation and records storage. Plan this before applying to DMAS.
checklist.cite: DBHDS DD Waivers Prospective Provider Toolkit

checklist.task: Decide your region (Northern Virginia vs. Rest of State) because the rate depends on it
checklist.instructions: DMAS publishes separate NOVA and ROS per diems. For a 4-or-fewer home at Tier 1 the rates are NOVA $391.16 and ROS $347.17. At Tier 2 they are NOVA $467.16 and ROS $414.60. Tier 4 is NOVA $616.89 and ROS $547.46. The model uses ROS rates. NOVA wages and rents were not researched, so build a separate budget if you choose NOVA.
checklist.cite: DMAS DD Waiver Services & Rates eff. 7/1/2026

checklist.task: Build your first-year working budget and revenue plan (also a licensing requirement)
checklist.instructions: 12VAC35-105-40 requires a working budget showing projected revenue and expenses for the first year, including a revenue plan. Use the DMAS H2022 per diem for your region and size, not private-pay prices. Include rent, staff coverage hours, insurance, a supervisor and billing. In the model, the one-home Tier 1 ROS configuration nets about $4,654/month (11.9% margin) at 92% occupancy. The Tier 2 home nets about $3,712 (8.0%). A Tier 4 home nets about $1,617 (2.7%). A two-home Tier 2 agency nets about $3,286 (3.5%). A three-home mixed-tier agency nets about $5,206 (3.6%).

checklist.task: Document funds or a line of credit covering at least 90 days of operating expenses
checklist.instructions: Non-government applicants (corporations, unincorporated organizations, sole proprietors, partnerships) must show funds or a line of credit sufficient to cover at least 90 days of operating expenses. Get a bank letter or line-of-credit commitment before you apply. The model estimates total cash needed at about $124,900 for a one-home configuration. It estimates about $310,250 for two homes and about $495,600 for three.

checklist.task: Understand how DMAS pays: per diem, fee-for-service, no room and board, minus patient pay
checklist.instructions: Group Home Residential is billed under H2022 as a per diem on a 344-billing-day basis. DD waiver benefits are carved out of managed care, and DMAS pays providers directly even for Cardinal Care members. DMAS does not reimburse room and board. DMAS pays only for services not covered by the person's patient pay amount. The exact conversion of 344 billing days into monthly units was not verified, and the model uses 28.67 days per month (344 ÷ 12).
checklist.cite: DD Waivers Manual Ch. IV; DMAS Cardinal Care DD fact sheet

checklist.task: Note the Medicaid six-licensed-bed limit and size every home to 4 or fewer beds at launch
checklist.instructions: 12VAC30-122-390 (per the Cornell LII mirror, so verify on LIS) limits reimbursed settings to six licensed beds, with older larger homes grandfathered. The DBHDS group home definition is 8 or fewer residents. The DMAS rate file shows rates for 4 through 12-person homes, but the rates fall as size rises: Tier 1 ROS is $347.17 for 4 or fewer persons, $281.88 for 8 persons and $242.64 for 12 persons. The model uses 4-bed homes only.

checklist.task: Do a demand check with your local Community Services Board (CSB)
checklist.instructions: The CSB is the entry point for DD waiver access, and individuals and families choose a provider through their support coordinator. The statewide waitlist was 14,226 in May 2026, with 2,632 Priority One on Sept. 21, 2026. No source ties that demand to a placement pipeline for a new provider. Call your local CSB's developmental services and support coordination staff, and ask what residential vacancies they cannot fill and which needs (Tier level, gender, location) are going unmet.
checklist.cite: My Life, My Community (CSB entry point); VBPD 2026 Assessments; DBHDS Item 295 K report

checklist.task: Review current rates and pending changes before locking your budget
checklist.instructions: The 7/1/2026 DMAS rate file includes a 2% increase for H2022. A further 4.6% on 1/1/2027 appears only in proposed budget amendments and is not confirmed as enacted. The enacted Item 291 raises only personal care, respite and companion rates (4% on 1/1/2027). Do not count on the 4.6%. Check the DMAS bulletin page for updates.

checklist.task: Check the pending DBHDS rule restructuring and track which version of the rules applies to you
checklist.instructions: DBHDS is restructuring Chapter 105 into one general chapter plus service-specific chapters, including a residential chapter. The general-chapter action was listed at the Proposed stage. Amendments from the 2025 regulatory reduction took effect June 18, 2025 per the Virginia Register. Re-check the current text of 12VAC35-105 on LIS before you finalize your policies.
checklist.cite: DBHDS licensing regulation overhaul memo; Town Hall action 6755

checklist.task: Select a home that suits a 4-resident, 24-hour supervised group home
checklist.instructions: The model assumes one 4-bedroom single-family house per home. The group home definition is a congregate service providing 24-hour supervision in a community-based home with eight or fewer residents. Choose a location near the day programs, medical care and transportation your residents will use. Do not sign a long lease until zoning and local use are confirmed and your DBHDS location is approved.

checklist.task: Budget rent realistically and treat it as a fixed cost
checklist.instructions: The model uses $2,500/month per 4-bedroom home as an operator estimate. It is based on a secondary summary of HUD FY2026 FMR data for Virginia Beach-Norfolk (4BR $2,290) plus a premium, and sources conflict on the official figures. Get local listings and confirm with HUD's official table. Rent applies whether the beds are full or not.

checklist.task: Plan bedrooms so no more than two individuals share a room
checklist.instructions: Under 12VAC35-105, no more than four individuals may share a bedroom, except in group homes, where no more than two may share a room. The text was published in the June 2024 final regulation. Confirm that this is still current after the June 2025 amendments. Single bedrooms make admission easier for most families.

checklist.task: Confirm the building, fire and life-safety requirements and the evacuation plan for your home
checklist.instructions: 12VAC35-105-260 and -320 (physical environment) were not retrieved in this research, so read them on LIS. Contact the local fire marshal and building official about smoke and CO alarms, extinguishers, egress and accessibility. Staffing must be sufficient to safely evacuate all individuals during an emergency (12VAC35-105-590), so the plan should match the home's layout and residents' mobility.

checklist.task: Design the home to meet CMS HCBS settings expectations
checklist.instructions: New DD group home providers must be in full compliance with the CMS HCBS settings regulations before completing the DMAS participation agreement. Plan for resident choice, privacy, lockable bedrooms where appropriate, visitors, and access to the community. Do not set up the house as an institution. DMAS issues an HCBS compliance letter before enrollment.
checklist.cite: CMS HCBS settings rule; DBHDS Prospective Provider Toolkit

checklist.task: Furnish and equip the home
checklist.instructions: The model assumes about $6,000 per home for furniture, beds, appliances and housewares, and $1,500 per home for safety and accessibility items. Both are operator estimates. Furnish to your residents' needs and let them add personal belongings.

checklist.task: Arrange a reliable vehicle
checklist.instructions: Residents need transport to appointments, day services and outings. The model carries $800/month per home (payment, insurance, fuel) as an operator estimate. Verify auto insurance covers business use and transport of residents, and that drivers have valid licenses.

checklist.task: Get quotes for liability and property insurance
checklist.instructions: No required insurance minimums were found in the 12VAC35-105 or 12VAC30-122 text retrieved (12VAC35-105-220 on indemnity coverage is listed but was not retrieved, so read it). Ask brokers about general and professional liability, abuse and molestation, property, auto and workers' comp. The model uses $500/month per home as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Understand the license types and limits for a new provider
checklist.instructions: A conditional license for a new provider may not exceed six months, and a conditional license plus renewals runs 12 months total. A group home provider on a conditional license is limited to a single location serving no more than four individuals. In January 2026 DBHDS clarified that a provider may hold only one active conditional license at a time. A full license may run up to three years, at the commissioner's discretion.

checklist.task: Create your account on the DBHDS CONNECT provider portal
checklist.instructions: New applications and license modifications are submitted electronically through CONNECT. For technical help, email licensingconnectinquiry@dbhds.virginia.gov and allow up to two business days for a response. Read the new applicant resources on the Office of Licensing page first.

checklist.task: Review the DBHDS Office of Licensing new applicant packet
checklist.instructions: The 2022 packet lists the license type 'developmental disability residential group home service for adults' (DD Group Home service 01) under 12VAC35-105-40(A). It is a 2022 document, so check it against current CONNECT instructions and the current regulation text.
checklist.cite: DBHDS Office of Licensing New Applicant Packet (2022)

checklist.task: Prepare the per-service application documents
checklist.instructions: 12VAC35-105-40 requires an application listing each service to be provided. For each service you need a staffing plan, employee credentials and job descriptions, a service description and a records management policy. Prepare them in a shared folder first, then upload them to CONNECT. The model budgets $2,000–$8,000 for policies, the staffing plan and the working budget, as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Write the provider staffing plan
checklist.instructions: Under 12VAC35-105-590 the provider must implement a written staffing plan covering the types, roles and numbers of staff. The plan must include enough staff to safely evacuate all individuals in an emergency. No numeric ratio or awake-overnight rule was verified. The model assumes 36, 48 or 72 staff-hours a day depending on Tier, as operator estimates. If your plan requires two overnight staff, add about 365 hours/month per home.

checklist.task: Name a qualified DD services supervisor and document the qualification
checklist.instructions: Supervision of developmental services must be provided by a person with at least one year of documented experience in direct DD services. A bachelor's degree in a human services field may be substituted by experience (follow the exact rule text). Administrator qualification and training hours (12VAC35-105-200, -410) were not verified, so read them before you hire.

checklist.task: Pay the DBHDS application fee shown in CONNECT (amount not verified)
checklist.instructions: The adult DD group home initial application fee was not confirmed on an official page. A secondary site says $750, and a $500 fee on a DBHDS page applies to children's residential providers. Do not budget from either. Use the fee CONNECT displays at submission. Note the date and method of payment.

checklist.task: Submit the application and track it in CONNECT
checklist.instructions: No processing or decision timelines for initial DD group home licenses were found in 12VAC35-105-40 or -50, so do not rely on any posted timeline from a third party. Check CONNECT regularly, answer requests promptly, and plan cash for at least the 90-day operating reserve while waiting.

checklist.task: Prepare for the licensing onsite review (frequency and process not verified)
checklist.instructions: 12VAC35-105-70 (onsite review) was not fetched. Read it on LIS. Make sure policies, the staffing plan, personnel files, background check records and emergency procedures are ready in the home and available electronically.

checklist.task: Plan your location and capacity under the conditional license
checklist.instructions: During the conditional period you are limited to a single location and no more than four individuals, and DBHDS allows one active conditional license per provider. That is why the launch configurations are single 4-bed homes. Do not sign a second lease or advertise a second home until you hold a full license.

checklist.task: Know how to change services, locations or ownership after licensure
checklist.instructions: Modification applications under 12VAC35-105-60 must be submitted at least 30 days before the proposed change. Licenses do not transfer: a change in ownership requires a new application and a new license. Do not sell or restructure ownership of the LLC without checking this first.

checklist.phase: PHASE 5 — POLICIES, HUMAN RIGHTS & COMPLIANCE SYSTEMS
checklist.task: Develop human rights-compliant policies and get them approved before licensure
checklist.instructions: Prior to receiving a DBHDS license, new providers must develop policies that comply with the Human Rights Regulations. Per the toolkit, email your Complaint Resolution Policy and the Human Rights Compliance Verification Checklist to the DBHDS Office of Human Rights. Follow the exact submission instructions in the toolkit.
checklist.cite: DBHDS DD Waivers Prospective Provider Toolkit

checklist.phase: PHASE 5 — POLICIES, HUMAN RIGHTS & COMPLIANCE SYSTEMS
checklist.task: Write the records management policy and set up a records system
checklist.instructions: A records management policy is a required per-service application item. For billing and authorizations, the support coordinator submits service authorization requests through the DBHDS Waiver Management System, so your records must match the person's authorized plan. No specific records or EHR software is mandated in the sources reviewed. The model carries $60/resident/month for records, billing software and exclusion screening as an operator estimate.

checklist.phase: PHASE 5 — POLICIES, HUMAN RIGHTS & COMPLIANCE SYSTEMS
checklist.task: Set up monthly federal exclusion screening (LEIE) for all staff and contractors
checklist.instructions: Providers must screen and document the names of all new and existing employees and contractors against the federal exclusion lists every month. Keep dated screening records. An excluded person on your payroll puts your Medicaid payments at risk.
checklist.cite: DBHDS DD Waivers Prospective Provider Toolkit

checklist.phase: PHASE 5 — POLICIES, HUMAN RIGHTS & COMPLIANCE SYSTEMS
checklist.task: Write emergency, evacuation and incident procedures matched to your staffing plan
checklist.instructions: Staffing must be sufficient to safely evacuate all individuals during an emergency. Build drills, evacuation routes, and procedures for medical emergencies and serious incidents. Read the DBHDS rules on emergency preparedness and serious incident reporting in 12VAC35-105 (not retrieved in this research) and add them to your policies.

checklist.phase: PHASE 5 — POLICIES, HUMAN RIGHTS & COMPLIANCE SYSTEMS
checklist.task: Write a room-and-board and patient pay procedure
checklist.instructions: DMAS does not reimburse room and board, and it pays only for services not covered by the person's patient pay amount. No Virginia cap or standard amount for room and board was found, and no SSI state supplement was verified. The 2026 SSI federal benefit rate is $994/month for an individual. The model assumes $700/month of room and board as an operator estimate. Put each person's charge in writing with their representative, and check their income and patient pay first.
checklist.cite: DD Waivers Manual Ch. IV; SSA 2026

checklist.phase: PHASE 5 — POLICIES, HUMAN RIGHTS & COMPLIANCE SYSTEMS
checklist.task: Know that EVV is not required for individuals in a DBHDS-licensed group home
checklist.instructions: DMAS's EVV FAQ says EVV is not required for individuals in a group home licensed by DBHDS. EVV rules are in 12VAC30-60-65. Re-check the FAQ if you add other services such as personal care or respite, which are covered by EVV.

checklist.task: Run fingerprint criminal history and Central Registry checks before any staff member works
checklist.instructions: DBHDS-licensed providers must run fingerprint-based criminal history checks on employees, students, interns, volunteers and contractors under Va. Code §§ 37.2-416 and 37.2-408.1. Results must be received before the person is permitted to work. Applicants also need a child abuse and neglect check through the VDSS Central Registry. Fingerprint vendor fees were not verified, so budget $300–$1,500 at launch as an operator estimate.
checklist.cite: Va. Code §§ 37.2-416, 37.2-408.1; DBHDS Background Investigations Unit

checklist.task: Use the $25 name and sex offender search for contractors, interns, students and volunteers
checklist.instructions: DBHDS charges $25.00 per search for those groups, paid by organization check or money order payable to Treasurer of Virginia. Follow the unit's current submission instructions. Questions go to the CONNECT help desk email.

checklist.task: Set wages at or above Virginia's minimum wage, and benchmark locally
checklist.instructions: Virginia's minimum wage is $12.77/hour in 2026. A secondary source says it rises to $13.75 on Jan. 1, 2027 under current statute, so verify on LIS. A secondary source says no city or county sets a higher local minimum. The model's $18.47 wage for direct support is the Richmond MSA mean for personal care and service occupations (May 2025). Virginia Beach is $17.87 and healthcare support there is $18.48. These are group-level proxies, because occupation-level wages for direct support professionals were not retrieved. Northern Virginia wages were not retrieved either.

checklist.task: Hire direct support professionals to cover the schedule in your staffing plan
checklist.instructions: The model assumes 36 staff-hours/day for Tier 1, 48 for Tier 2 and 72 for Tier 4 (operator estimates, not rule ratios). That works out to 1,095, 1,460 and 2,190 hours/month. Hire enough staff to fill every shift, plus relief for call-offs. Payroll taxes, workers' comp and benefits add about 19.5% in the model.

checklist.task: Meet the DD waiver staff training and competency requirements
checklist.instructions: Staff providing group home residential service must meet the provider training and competency requirements in 12VAC30-122-180. Pre-service and annual training hours and administrator training hours were not verified (a secondary '40 hours' claim is unconfirmed). Read 12VAC30-122-180 and 12VAC35-105-440/-450 and document each staff member's training before they work alone with residents. The model budgets $200/month per home for training and checks.

checklist.task: Hire or designate the program director and a billing coordinator
checklist.instructions: The model carries a 0.5 FTE supervisor for single homes, 1.0 FTE plus a 0.5 FTE billing coordinator for two homes, and 1.0 FTE supervisor, 0.5 FTE assistant and 0.75 FTE billing coordinator for three homes. Salaries are operator estimates, since occupation-level wages for managers were not retrieved. An owner can fill the supervisor role if they meet the one-year DD experience rule.

checklist.task: Set up payroll, I-9 and personnel files
checklist.instructions: Keep a file for each employee with background check results, training certificates, credentials and the monthly exclusion screening. Use a payroll service. The model budgets accounting and payroll service within $500/month for one home.

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — DMAS PROVIDER ENROLLMENT & BILLING SETUP
checklist.task: Complete the DMAS provider participation agreement for Group Home Residential
checklist.instructions: All providers of group home residential service must have a current DMAS provider participation agreement. Per DBHDS, new DD group home residential providers must be in full compliance with the CMS HCBS settings rules before completing it. Follow the DMAS provider enrollment steps in the DD Waivers Manual Chapter 2. Virginia-specific enrollment steps beyond that were not fully verified.

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — DMAS PROVIDER ENROLLMENT & BILLING SETUP
checklist.task: Get the DMAS HCBS compliance letter before enrollment
checklist.instructions: The toolkit says a DMAS HCBS compliance letter is needed before DMAS enrollment. Follow the toolkit steps to request it, and keep the letter with your licensing file.
checklist.cite: DBHDS DD Waivers Prospective Provider Toolkit

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — DMAS PROVIDER ENROLLMENT & BILLING SETUP
checklist.task: Pay the federal enrollment application fee if your enrollment notice requires it
checklist.instructions: CMS set a $750 application fee for institutional Medicaid providers that enroll for the first time, required with applications submitted between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31, 2026. DMAS says institutional providers may owe a federally required fee at the time of application, and the enrollment notice states whether it applies. Pay only if the notice says so. Applications submitted in 2027 will carry the 2027 amount.
checklist.cite: CMS Federal Register notice (CY2026); DD Waivers Manual Chapter 2

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — DMAS PROVIDER ENROLLMENT & BILLING SETUP
checklist.task: Obtain an organizational NPI (if the DMAS enrollment packet requires it)
checklist.instructions: Check the enrollment instructions in Chapter 2. If an NPI is required, apply through NPPES, which is free, with the legal entity name matching your SCC and IRS records. The NPI requirement was not separately verified in this research.

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — DMAS PROVIDER ENROLLMENT & BILLING SETUP
checklist.task: Learn the billing code and size modifiers
checklist.instructions: Group Home Residential is H2022. Modifiers by home size are UA (4 or fewer), U2 (5), U3 (6), U4 (7), U5 (8), U6 (9), U7 (10), U8 (11) and U9 (12). Bill the modifier that matches your licensed home size, and bill the tier on the person's service authorization. Tier criteria are in 12VAC30-122-210, which was not summarized in this research.

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — DMAS PROVIDER ENROLLMENT & BILLING SETUP
checklist.task: Understand the service authorization process before admitting anyone
checklist.instructions: Service authorization requests for DD waiver services go through the DBHDS Waiver Management System, submitted by the individual's support coordinator. You cannot bill without an authorization in place. Work with the support coordinator on the start date and the authorized tier. Do not admit a resident on a verbal promise.

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — DMAS PROVIDER ENROLLMENT & BILLING SETUP
checklist.task: Set up claim submission and a reconciliation routine
checklist.instructions: DD waiver claims are paid fee-for-service by DMAS, not by Cardinal Care managed care plans. Reconcile each claim against authorizations and patient pay. Rates are on a 344-billing-day basis, and the exact conversion to monthly units was not verified, so confirm the billing rules in the DMAS manual and your remittance statements.
checklist.cite: DMAS Cardinal Care DD fact sheet; DD Waivers Manual Chapter IV

checklist.phase: PHASE 7 — DMAS PROVIDER ENROLLMENT & BILLING SETUP
checklist.task: Subscribe to DMAS bulletins and rate updates
checklist.instructions: DMAS announced July 1, 2026 rate updates in a provider bulletin under Item 291 of the 2026 Appropriation Act. DMAS also says it is requesting authority for DD and HCBS waiver amendments effective Jan. 1, 2027, so watch the waivers page and the bulletin list for changes that affect group homes.
checklist.cite: DMAS provider bulletin; DMAS waivers page

checklist.task: Build referral relationships with local CSBs and support coordinators
checklist.instructions: The CSB is the first contact for DD waiver access, and support coordinators help individuals and families pick a provider. Introduce your home, tier focus, location and openings to developmental services directors and support coordinators at nearby CSBs. The model carries $150/month for outreach as an operator estimate. No referral-source breakdown was found, so track your own.
checklist.cite: My Life, My Community (CSB entry point)

checklist.task: Understand where slots come from and set realistic fill expectations
checklist.instructions: Across the three DD waivers there were 21,479 funded slots at the end of FY 2026. Vacated slots were reassigned from the waitlist 635 times in FY 2026, and turnover of existing slots totaled 861. DBHDS says that falls far short of the Priority One need. By Sept. 8, 2026, 77% of FY 2026 new-slot recipients had a service authorized. The model assumes one new resident a month and 92% occupancy as operator assumptions, so each month of slow filling adds a month of fixed costs.
checklist.cite: DBHDS Item 295 K DD Waiver Services Report (2026)

checklist.task: Run a resident-matching and admission process
checklist.instructions: Meet the individual, family and support coordinator. Review the person's plan, authorized tier, behavioral and medical needs, and compatibility with current housemates before accepting. Verify that your staffing plan covers the needs. A mismatch causes crisis calls and staffing overruns. Tier 4 homes in the model earn only about 2.7% margin at default occupancy, so check complex needs before accepting.

checklist.task: Collect the person's income information and set room and board and spending money
checklist.instructions: DMAS does not pay room and board, and patient pay reduces what DMAS pays. Collect the person's SSI or other income documents and set a written charge that leaves personal spending money. The 2026 SSI federal benefit is $994/month, and no Virginia state supplement amount was verified. The model assumes $700/month.
checklist.cite: DD Waivers Manual Ch. IV; SSA 2026

checklist.task: Track occupancy against your break-even
checklist.instructions: At the model's default occupancy of 92%, break-even occupancy is about 80.5% for the one-home Tier 1 model, 84.3% for the one-home Tier 2 model, 88.6% for the two-home and three-home models, and 89.5% for the Tier 4 home. Every month a bed is empty, rent and staff cost the same. Track occupancy weekly.

checklist.task: Stress-test staffing and rate assumptions after the first 90 days
checklist.instructions: If DBHDS or your plan requires two awake overnight staff, add about 365 hours per month per home, which would erase the single-home margin. A 4.6% group home increase on 1/1/2027 is not enacted, so do not plan on it. Re-run your budget with actual hours, authorizations and patient pay.

checklist.task: File license renewals at least 30 calendar days before expiration
checklist.instructions: DBHDS guidance (Jan. 2026) says renewal applications must be submitted at least 30 calendar days before expiration. Late renewals risk denied DMAS claims. A full license may run up to three years. The renewal fee was not verified, and the model carries a $63/month placeholder per site (about $750/year). Replace it with the actual fee.

checklist.task: Convert the conditional license to a full license before the 12-month cap
checklist.instructions: A conditional license may not exceed six months, and renewals are capped at 12 months total. Know your end date, and work with the Office of Licensing early so that you are not left without a license. Keep records showing compliance throughout the conditional period.

checklist.task: Keep monthly exclusion screening, background checks and training current for all staff
checklist.instructions: Document monthly federal exclusion screening, pre-hire background checks for all new staff, interns, students and volunteers, and ongoing staff training and competency records. Put reminders in your calendar and audit them quarterly.
checklist.cite: DBHDS Toolkit; DBHDS Background Investigations Unit; 12VAC30-122-180

checklist.task: File modifications before changing locations, services or capacity
checklist.instructions: Submit modification applications in CONNECT at least 30 days before the change. A new home or added service is a modification, and it must fit within the conditional or full license limits. Moving to a new house is a location change, so do not move residents before approval.

checklist.task: Keep the staffing plan current and test emergency evacuation
checklist.instructions: Update the written staffing plan whenever residents' needs, tiers or the number of residents change, and conduct and document evacuation drills. Staffing must be enough to evacuate all individuals safely.

checklist.task: Pay the SCC annual registration fee and keep entity records current
checklist.instructions: A secondary source puts the Virginia LLC annual registration fee at $50, with a $25 late penalty. Confirm with the SCC, and set a calendar reminder. The model carries about $4/month.

checklist.task: Monitor regulatory changes
checklist.instructions: Watch the Virginia Register, Town Hall and DBHDS Office of Licensing notices. The Chapter 105 restructuring (general chapter plus a residential chapter) could change numbering and requirements. Update your policies after each final action.
checklist.cite: DBHDS Overhaul memo; Town Hall action 6755

checklist.task: Review the minimum wage and payroll rates each January
checklist.instructions: The 2026 minimum wage is $12.77. A secondary source lists a scheduled increase to $13.75 on Jan. 1, 2027, so verify on LIS. Re-run staff costs, since direct support is the largest cost in the model.

checklist.task: Decide when to add a second and third home
checklist.instructions: The two-home Tier 2 model nets about $3,286/month (3.5%) and the three-home mixed model about $5,206/month (3.6%), both lower in margin than the one-home models because of full-time supervisor, assistant and billing costs. The single Tier 1 home is the highest-margin model at 11.9%. Add homes only after the first home is full, the license is full status, and cash is available. The model estimates cash needed at about $310,250 for two homes and $495,600 for three.

checklist.task: Open homes one at a time
checklist.instructions: The workbook staffs every home from month 1, which overstates cash needs if you open homes in sequence. Hire staff as each home fills. Each new location needs its own modification or license approval and its own DMAS and HCBS readiness.

checklist.task: Evaluate other waiver residential options only after licensing is stable
checklist.instructions: DMAS also publishes rates for Supported Living Residential (H0043, Tier 1 NOVA $369.06 and ROS $327.54 per diem) and Sponsored Residential, which is a separate service. The FY2026 DBHDS report shows Sponsored Residential spending of $350,439,439 for 3,097 individuals. These are different services with different requirements. Research them separately before adding them.
checklist.cite: DMAS rate file; DBHDS Item 295 K report
